keyVerseText: By thee have I been holden up from the womb: thou art he that took me out of my mother's bowels: my praise shall be continually of thee.
rootMeaning: The root of גָּזָה (gâzâh) is related to the primitive root גּוּז (gûwz), which carries the core idea of cutting off or shearing away. This root conveys a sense of separation or severing, not merely in a physical sense but also metaphorically, such as the passing away or removal of something. The literal root sense emphasizes an active, deliberate action of taking or cutting out, which enriches the English gloss 'take' by highlighting the intentionality and decisive nature of the act.
usageInScripture: This Hebrew verb appears only once in Scripture, in Psalms 71:6, where it is translated as 'thou art he that took.' The singular occurrence and consistent translation suggest a focused and specific use, emphasizing God’s active role in bringing or taking the psalmist out from the womb. The word’s rarity underlines its significance in this intimate context of divine intervention and care.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding גָּזָה as 'to cut off' or 'to take out' deepens our appreciation of God’s sovereign and personal involvement in human life, especially from its very beginning. It portrays God not as a distant creator but as one who actively and intentionally forms and separates the individual for His purposes. This verb reflects the intimate craftsmanship of God, who holds authority over life and destiny, underscoring the Christian belief in God’s providential care and sustaining power. It also points to the theme of being chosen and set apart by God, foundational to the identity of believers in Christ.
keyVerseReflection: Psalm 71:6 declares, 'By thee have I been holden up from the womb: thou art he that took me out of my mother's bowels.' The use of גָּזָה here highlights God's deliberate action in bringing the psalmist into life, emphasizing divine protection and care from the very start. This word enriches the verse by portraying God as the one who actively and purposefully secures life, inspiring continual praise and trust in His sustaining power.
